views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Continue pressing the negotiation inside the 90-day G20 truce window rather than escalating or conceding. Keep the ~$250B of Section 301 tariffs in place as leverage, demand enforceable purchase commitments plus structural IP/forced-transfer reform, and hold the suspended 10%-to-25% List 3 escalation as a credible March 1 stick — but do not trigger it without exhausting the talks, since escalation now would break the truce, roil already-volatile markets, and deepen farm-belt losses ahead of the March deadline.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to US interests is real but modest-to-favorable, not existential. The US holds the negotiating initiative and the opponent is under visible pressure: China is posting its slowest growth since 1990 and Huawei faces DOJ charges (timeline: 2019-01-28), giving Washington leverage to extract IP and purchase concessions. Yet costs are concrete: US soybean sales to China have fallen ~94%, farm bankruptcies are rising across the Midwest, and a $12B aid program has paid out little (NYT/Reason/Politico). US consumer sentiment fell from 100.1 to 91.2 and markets were turbulent in Q4 (UMCSENT series), signalling that further escalation, not de-escalation, is the risky path. Lighthizer has signaled the March 1 deadline will not be extended, and China has reportedly not tabled anything substantively new (Politico, Jan 29; US-China Business Council). That combination argues for holding firm and negotiating hard for a verifiable deal while keeping the tariff lever credible — hence a mildly negative threat reading (-0.2) and a mild negotiate stance (+0.15), consistent with neither breaking the truce nor surrendering leverage.
key_factors: ~$250B of Chinese imports under Section 301 tariffs; List 3 held at 10% under the truce
March 1 expiry of 90-day G20 window; Lighthizer signals no extension
Soybean exports to China down ~94%; farm-belt bankruptcies rising (political exposure)
US consumer sentiment 100.1 -> 91.2 and elevated Q4 market volatility
Huawei/Meng DOJ charges (Jan 28) add legal friction with allies but are held separate from talks
China's slowing growth gives the US negotiation leverage on IP/purchase commitments

sources_cited.excerpt: G20 Buenos Aires: Trump and Xi agree to 90-day negotiation window; Jan 1 List 3 hike to 25% suspended (tariffs remain at 10%).
US DOJ unseals fraud and sanctions-related charges against Huawei and Meng; formal extradition request.
Lighthizer and Mnuchin in Beijing for high-level talks; purchase commitments discussed; enforcement and structural IP issues unresolved.
US consumer sentiment fell from 100.1 (Sep) to 91.2 (Jan).
Lighthizer signals March 1 tariff deadline will not be extended; US business council says China has not tabled anything substantively new.
US soybean exports to China down ~40% year over year (94% decline in sales to China vs prior harvest); $12B aid paid out little; farm bankruptcies rising.
